pl-l4d49c2-d1e115.summary: Asks whether one of greater merit, like Peter, knows something of God that one of lesser merit, like Linus, does not.

pl-l4d49c2-d1e118.summary: Reports the view of many that all the elect know everything about God pertaining to beatitude, but differently: nothing knowable in God seems greater than understanding him three and one, which all will then know by sight; so nothing pertaining to beatitude will be unknown to any of the blessed, but they will differ in the manner of seeing, some shining more and others less.
claims: All the blessed see the Trinity.
They differ in how clearly they see.

pl-l4d49c2.summary: Asks whether a more meritorious saint, like Peter, knows something of God that a less meritorious one, like Linus, does not. Many hold that all the elect know everything about God pertaining to beatitude, but differently: nothing knowable in God is greater than his being three and one, which all will see; so nothing pertaining to beatitude is unknown to any of the blessed, though they differ in the manner of seeing, some shining more than others.
claims: All the blessed know all that pertains to beatitude.
They differ in the manner and clarity of knowing.
